transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09
Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Orion Head of ML), Amir Qureshi (Orion PM), Dr. Rahul Menon (Clinical Lead), Samira Khan (Orion Dev)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in focused on quality evaluation and regression triage. Reviewed recent eval results, discussed prompt-set regressions for clinical note summarization, guardrail false positives, and next steps for re-scoring and guardrail tuning. Agreed on data deliverables and a re-run of the eval harness with adjusted thresholds.

Topics covered:
- Recent eval results (precision/recall drift on adverse-event extraction)
- Prompt set changes and candidate rollbacks
- Guardrail tuning: regex vs model-based classifiers vs rule-engine
- Scoring thresholds and mismatch between human labels and automated scoring
- Fallback & routing plan (smaller model vs cached completions)
- Action items and timelines

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription has typical Fireflies artifacts):
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We have about 40 minutes, lots to chew through on the eval results. Marcus, do you want to kick with the high-level numbers?
[00:18] Marcus Li: Yeah, sure. Uh, so the 5/7 sweep we ran against the 4k validation set, overall F1 for the adverse-event extraction went from 0.82 down to 0.74 after the prompt tweaks we shipped last week. The drop is mostly in recall on the 'medication-reaction' bucket.
[00:35] Lena Ortiz: Wait, that big? We saw some drops locally but not that severe. Are you sure it's the prompt and not the scoring change?
[00:46] Marcus Li: Good question. There's two differences: 1) we tightened the scoring threshold for partial matches, and 2) we introduced one-shot priming to reduce hallucinations. The one-shot decreased hallucinations but also made the model more conservative.
[01:05] Amir Qureshi: Can you remind us what the threshold was before and now? I think our internal annotators were scoring partial entity matches as 0.6 before?
[01:15] Marcus Li: Previously the overlap metric used a 0.5 F-score threshold for fuzzy matching; we moved it to 0.65 which knocks out borderline partials.
[01:26] Dr. Rahul Menon: From a clinical safety POV I'd rather have fewer false positives, but I'm worried about missing legitimate adverse events. The downstream triage depends on recall.
[01:38] Priya Shah: Right, so it's a tradeoff. The objective for this POC was to keep recall above 0.75 for the adverse bucket. We missed that bar this run.
[01:48] Sofia Alvarez: Quick note — the JSON export of the eval results had a mismatched column header, so some of the percents we saw in the deck were flipped, that may have confused earlier readings. Apologies for that noise.
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: OK ok, that explains part of it. Marcus, can you surface an example of a false negative and a false positive from the current run?
[02:15] Marcus Li: Yeah, I'll paste two snippets in the shared doc after the call but quick example — FN: clinical note says "patient developed a maculopapular rash after starting lamotrigine" and model returned a generic skin-irritation tag but didn't link to medication reaction. FP: model flagged "elevated liver enzymes" as a drug-related AE when the note clearly said baseline LFT elevation.
[02:38] Amir Qureshi: Are those in the labeled regression set? We tried to send edge-cases last sprint but maybe the format didn't map.
[02:47] Samira Khan: We uploaded them but there was a csv header mismatch; their columns were var_name vs label vs notes and Redwood expected label, text. I can fix that and re-upload today.
[02:59] Priya Shah: Great. Action: Samira to reupload correct CSV.
[03:06] Marcus Li: Another point — the guardrail rule we dropped in was pattern-based to catch 'contraindicated' mentions, but it was too broad and triggered on phrases like "no contraindications observed" — so it created false positives. We have a regex fix but it needs to be more context aware.
[03:27] Dr. Rahul Menon: Regex is brittle for clinical negation; we should consider a model-based classifier for negation detection or leverage dependency parsing.
[03:36] Marcus Li: Totally, but model-based detector increases inference cost. We can do a hybrid: fast regex for obvious cases and an optional model-run for ambiguous sentences.
[03:50] Priya Shah: That aligns with the cost/latency tradeoffs we discussed — Redwood can route ambiguous cases to a different path, e.g. a smaller specialized classifier or fall back to cached completions if we recently processed similar notes.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: Can you explain how caching would work for our use case? We worry about stale annotations.
[04:13] Marcus Li: Sure. Prefix/KV caching — so if the note includes a repeating patient history pattern, we can serve cached inference for repeated chunks. But for unique clinical events we wouldn't cache. Also cache invalidation policies tie to patient visit IDs. Note: in some earlier notes the transcript reads KV cash which is a little weird in export.
[04:33] Amir Qureshi: And latency? If we route to the model-based negation detector what's the added time?
[04:40] Marcus Li: On our Dedicated config it's ~60-90ms extra median for the small classifier; on Hosted it's ~120-200ms depending on load.
[04:50] Samira Khan: That is acceptable for our nightly batch but not for real-time triage. Our realtime SLA is 500ms end-to-end.
[04:58] Priya Shah: We can gate it — real-time path stays conservative (prefer recall), while batch re-processing can re-score with heavier detectors and update flags.
[05:10] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Next topic — prompt-set regressions. We saw a drop after swapping the few-shot exemplars; what exactly changed in the prompt packing?
[05:20] Marcus Li: We removed two long exemplars to reduce context length and added a single one-shot plus system instruction emphasizing conciseness. That reduced hallucinations but apparently reduced recall on long, multi-event notes because the exemplar variety decreased.
[05:36] Amir Qureshi: So revert to previous exemplars? Or do a mixed A/B test?
[05:42] Marcus Li: Recommend an A/B where A = previous few-shot with looser scoring, B = current few-shot with higher scoring threshold. We can run this across the 10k sample and measure delta by subgroup (medication-related, device errors, lab abnormalities).
[05:58] Dr. Rahul Menon: Please include per-subgroup recall/precision; we need to see impact on the meds bucket separately.
[06:06] Priya Shah: Marcus, can you run the A/B and push results before next sync?
[06:10] Marcus Li: Yes, aiming to have preliminary by 2025-07-16.
[06:15] Sonia (note: misspelled sometimes)
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Another item — the human labeler instructions might be inconsistent: some labelers count any mention of reaction even if historical, others only count events within the visit. That would explain recall mismatch.
[06:34] Amir Qureshi: Good catch. I'll audit the label instructions and send clarifying guidance.
[06:40] Samira Khan: We noticed a few borderline cases where the model used templated language and the scoring penalized synonyms. Maybe we need normalized canonicalization in scoring.
[06:52] Marcus Li: We can add a synonym map for common clinical terms (e.g., "elevated LFTs" -> "liver enzyme elevation") to improve fuzzy matching. Adds negligible overhead to eval.
[07:03] Priya Shah: Let's include that in the eval pipeline.
[07:07] 
[07:12] Marcus Li: Quick note on regression detection — we observed that small prompt changes can cause subtle distribution shifts. To catch that earlier I recommend instrumenting a lightweight canary that runs on new prompt commits against a 500-example regression set. If the performance delta exceeds X, block rollout.
[07:32] Lena Ortiz: That sounds good, what threshold X are you proposing?
[07:36] Marcus Li: Initially proposing 0.03 absolute F1 drop on critical buckets. Can tweak after first few runs.
[07:44] Amir Qureshi: 3 points seems reasonable.
[07:48] Priya Shah: Make that configurable.
[07:51] Marcus Li: Sure. We'll add it as a parameter in the rollout policy.
[07:55] 
[08:00] Dr. Rahul Menon: On guardrails, do you support audit logs for every triggered rule? We need traceability for compliance.
[08:08] Marcus Li: Yes — Redwood Console captures rule triggers, full request/response hashes, and model variant used. The private deployment adds capability to retain logs to your retention policies and integrate with your KMS/HSM for log encryption.
[08:24] Lena Ortiz: Encryption at rest is mandatory for us. We also need SSO/SAML and role-based access.
[08:31] Priya Shah: All included in the Private package; Dedicated has RBAC and audit trails as part of the offering. We'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs after this call — action for Priya.
[08:43] Sofia Alvarez: I'll attach the compliance pack to the workspace in case anyone needs it.
[08:49] 
[09:00] Amir Qureshi: One subtle regression we noticed — the model started truncating long medication lists in the generated summary after the prompt change. Is that a tokenization/context-length issue?
[09:12] Marcus Li: Probably. We changed the truncation policy to preserve system instruction and exemplars which pushed real content out on very long notes. We can either increase max tokens for the generation or compress exemplars (use shorter paraphrased exemplars).
[09:27] Samira Khan: Increasing max tokens is fine in Dedicated but might bump cost for Hosted POC. We prefer exemplar compression if it retains quality.
[09:36] Marcus Li: We'll trial paraphrase compression via automatic distillation and compare.
[09:41] 
[09:44] Priya Shah: Ok checklist recap — Samira re-upload corrected CSV; Marcus run A/B on 10k with subgroup metrics and synonym map; Marcus also implement canary threshold in rollout policy; Priya to send compliance pack and prompt diffs.
[09:59] Lena Ortiz: Also please add examples of false positives and false negatives to the shared doc with line numbers. That will help annotator audit.
[10:07] Marcus Li: Will do.
[10:10] Amir Qureshi: One operational question — if we want to pin a model version in Dedicated vs Hosted, how do rollbacks work?
[10:19] Priya Shah: We support canary + automatic rollback on threshold breach. If pinned, rolling back is just a config change but we recommend not pinning during early POC so A/B can run.
[10:30] Dr. Rahul Menon: For clinical use cases, we may want pinning once we hit stability.
[10:34] Priya Shah: Agree.
[10:36] 
[10:40] Sofia Alvarez: Quick note — transcription quality here may have a few misheard bits (e.g., KMS -> K M S, KV cache -> KV cash). Please rely on the shared doc for canonical examples.
[10:52] 
[11:00] Action item recap (verbal):
- Priya: Share prompt diffs, guardrail rule file, compliance pack (SOC2/ISO) - due 2025-07-11
- Marcus: A/B eval on 10k, subgroup metrics, synonym map, canary threshold implementation - due 2025-07-16
- Samira: Re-upload corrected CSV of regression edge cases, integrate SDK smoke test - due 2025-07-13
- Lena: Audit and clarify labeler instructions and return with decision - due 2025-07-14

[11:40] Priya Shah: Alright, if no other items let's wrap. Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene next week same time.
[11:48] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
